title: Mental health care for ADHD and autism with co-occurring needs
asked: Dr Hamid Razak asked whether the tiered-care mental health model includes people with neurodevelopmental conditions like ADHD and autism who also have mental health needs, and what clinical pathways and funding support are available in public psychiatric or psychological care.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon said the tiered-care model is organised by severity and complexity of mental health needs, not specific diagnoses, and applies to people with ADHD and autism who have co-occurring mental health needs. In the community, they can access free or subsidised services such as REACH for children, CHAT for adolescents and young adults, and CIHT for adults. Specialist psychiatric services at public Specialist Outpatient Clinics offer means-tested subsidies of up to 70% for eligible patients, including those with neuro-developmental conditions, and medical social workers can help with MediFund. On the supplementary, he said the National Mental Health Office works with social partners and can conduct awareness courses if capabilities need strengthening, and that counsellors who detect depression would be encouraged to refer onwards for specialist assessments and co-manage with higher-tier partners if needed.
